newsitem.title: UK: Britain identifies 17 human "mad cow" cases.
newsitem.headline: Britain identifies 17 human "mad cow" cases.

text.p: Britain's Health Ministry said on Monday it had identified 17 probable and definite cases of a new type of the brain-wasting Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (CJD) that has been linked with mad cow disease.

In a regular monthly update it said 17 cases of the "new variant" CJD, which doctors say probably was caused by eating beef infected with bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE or mad cow disease), had been seen since the new variant was identified in March 1996.
That makes one additional case since last month, but the Health Ministry did not say whether the new case was a probable or definite one.
One case of the new variant has been reported in France.
CJD normally strikes about one in a million. There were 57 cases in Britain last year.
It is always fatal and usually has a long incubation period. Scientists warn there could be an epidemic of CJD mirroring the BSE epidemic in British cattle but say it is too soon to know.
